won.source: UWF Gold Rush 2003; corroborated by the following broadcast's own commentary crediting Hawkins as the reigning champion entering his first defense.

note: Lost the title in his first defense, breaking his arm on a botched moonsault fall against a same-night replacement challenger, Chris O'Brien, on 9 August 2003.

Retained again on 20 December 2003 over Quinn Brown, pinning him with an accidental Ace Crusher counter off Brown's own inverted DDT attempt. title: uwf-mar96-womens-heavyweight-championship-of-the-world
label: Stephanie Harper

won.source: Stephanie Harper's own in-ring promo on 30 August 2003, stating she won the title at Gold Rush 2003 and would not lose it in her first defense; no surviving document states the match itself.

note: Retained against Bliss on 30 August 2003; promised a three-way defense against Nina Grimsson and Myra Benedict the following week after their own number-one-contender's match ended in a time-limit draw. Retained again on 25 October 2003, pinning Myra Benedict with the Fallen Star in the promised three-way dance after Nina Grimsson wrestled with open disinterest throughout. Retained again on 15 November 2003 by submission (Texas Cloverleaf) over challenger Donna Tetreault, who wrestled without Simon O'Neal at ringside after Vice-President Jessica Marshall barred him. Lost the title to that same challenger, Donna Tetreault, on 15 May 2004.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 May 2004: pinned by Donna Tetreault after a somersault plancha caught her and cornerman Simon O'Neal, with the referee's own ten count on both women having lapsed by the cover.

title: uwf-mar96-rampage-championship
label: Jamie Underwood

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 August 2004: Jamie Underwood pinned champion Uriah Hawkins with a small package after Papa Legba ran in and blindsided Hawkins with the Ragga Bomb.

note: Won the UWF Rampage Championship from Uriah Hawkins with interference from Papa Legba, who framed the run-in as payback for Hawkins costing him the UWF Meltdown Championship days earlier; 'son' Jamie Jr. and bodyguard Corporate Leverage also worked the ringside area, though the brass knuckles Leverage passed to Underwood went unused.

title: uwf-mar96-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Sons of Cacophony

won.source: The promotion's own billing and commentary on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 May 2005, and the Grimssons' own in-ring remarks that night, crediting the win to Rise to Power while avenging an attack on their own sister, Lisa Drake; that pre-show itself has no primary-source card text in the held record.

note: Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing and commentary; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which Erik and Chad Grimsson won the titles from the Privateers at Rise to Power. Retained the titles over the Privateers by pinfall (an inverted backslide DDT from Erik, the Metal Meltdown) in a rematch on 28 May 2005, with interference from Fury (Rage, Spice) disrupting the challengers. Lost the titles to the Hands of Death (Serge Annis, Caliban) in a bout not read by this collection, recapped by Alex Extreme's own tirade on UWF Meltdown, 20 July 2005.

lost.source: UWF Meltdown, 20 July 2005, and UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 23 July 2005: both broadcasts bill the Hands of Death as the current World Tag Team Champions, having taken the titles from the Sons of Cacophony on the previous week's own unread Rampage (9 July 2005); no surviving document in the held record states the match itself.

title: uwf-mar96-heavyweight-championship-of-the-world
label: Kyle Lee

won.source: UWF Gold Rush 2004, 5 June 2004: Kyle Lee pinned champion Michael Augustine with a second Gone to Texas in the main event triple threat, also involving Edmond Winston IV, after the real Alex Extreme knocked out both other competitors, having exposed an impostor Alex Extreme (Job Holly) who had been assisting Winston.

note: Won the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World from Michael Augustine in the Gold Rush 2004 main event triple threat, also involving Edmond Winston IV, capping a year-long rise from a non-wrestling authority-figure role to the sport's top title; embraced manager Tesla St. James in the ring afterward. Retained over Jamie Underwood by disqualification on 18 September 2004 after owner Edmond Winston IV struck him with a steel chair, then superplexed him from the top rope through a steel ladder propped against the ring apron; Tesla St. James was knocked out trying to fight Winston off. Retained again over "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez by pinfall (a surprise inside cradle) on 11 December 2004, denying Martinez the title and Luke Kinsey his own promised shot at it for Rise to Power.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 May 2005: pinned by Scott "Hotspot" Daniels (the Before the Fall piledriver) in an impromptu title defense forced by an Edmond Winston IV charter amendment, with Kari Stevens's own interference at ringside.

title: uwf-mar96-north-american-tag-team-championship
label: The Ghost Dancers

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 25 October 2003: stereo scorpion deathlocks forced Trevor Hextall to submit.

note: Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship from Team Canada; the same match's own fine print kept Team Canada's separate UWF World Tag Team Championship off the line.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 November 2003: the Sons of Cacaphony, Erik and Chad Grimsson, became the first complete tag team to escape the Tower of Doom, winning the title under the match's own stipulation.

title: uwf-mar96-north-american-tag-team-championship
label: The Sons of Cacaphony

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 November 2003: Erik and Chad Grimsson became the first complete tag team to escape the Tower of Doom cage, the match's own stipulation for the title.

note: Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship inside the Tower of Doom, a four-team cage-escape match, taking the belts from their own side's teammates and the reigning champions, the Ghost Dancers, by being the first complete pair out of the cage. Retained against the Universal Powers (Todd Franklin and Bobby Lincoln) on 21 March 2004, the Sky Hammer combination finishing Bobby Lincoln after both teams traded dives to the arena floor. Lost the title to the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln and Todd Franklin) in a street fight on 28 August 2004, an unidentified masked interloper knocking Erik Grimsson out from inside a locker-room closet before Todd Franklin's superkick finished him for the pin.

title: uwf-mar96-womens-tag-team-championship
label: Team BATTLE*DREAM

won.source: the promotion's own billing and commentary on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 11 June 2005, crediting Team BATTLE*DREAM with winning the title from the Bod Squad at the Rise to Power pre-show; that pre-show has no primary-source card text in the held record.

note: Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which the title changed hands from the Bod Squad. Ended on 11 June 2005 when Reona Yoshida left the UWF for Joshi Puroresu STARDOM in Japan; the reign continued unbroken under the pairing's new name, the Psychommunity, with Misaki Ishikawa's own older sister Naomi installed as the new co-champion.

title: uwf-mar96-north-american-heavyweight-championship
label: Eugene Robinson

won.source: the promotion's own billing on Saturday Night Rampage, 30 August 2003

note: Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing of this wrestler as champion; retained by a double-stoppage draw against Tragedy after Derek Irvin's interference on 30 August 2003. No surviving document in the held record states the match in which the title was won. Did not defend the title in a non-title six-man tag on 4 October 2003, then lost it to Kyle Lee by pinfall in a steel cage match on 25 October 2003.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 25 October 2003: pinned by Kyle Lee's Superfly Splash from the top of the steel cage.

title: uwf-mar96-north-american-tag-team-championship
label: The Universal Powers

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 August 2004, a street fight: an unidentified masked interloper knocked Erik Grimsson out from inside a locker-room closet, and Todd Franklin finished him with a superkick for the pin.

note: Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship from the Sons of Cacaphony in a street fight with the help of an unidentified masked interloper, whose identity was not revealed this show; the Privateers separately ambushed Chad Grimsson at ringside during the same match, unrelated to either tag team's own title challenge. Lost the title to the Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos Romani) by pinfall on 20 October 2004, Niklos pinning Lincoln with a neckbreaker off his own brother's shoulders after a returning Vyolynce's own ringside chair distraction.

title: uwf-mar96-meltdown-championship
label: Papa Legba

won.source: UWF Meltdown, 17 December 2003: Papa Legba beat Paul Wong in the finals of a fifteen-man battle royal and two-match tournament to become the first-ever UWF Meltdown Champion.

note: Won the inaugural UWF Meltdown Championship, surviving a fifteen-man battle royal as one of its own final four, beating Victor Frost in the semi-finals with an inverted DDT, then Paul Wong in the finals with the Black Magic superbomb. Retained against Alex Kidd on 10 March 2004 by pinfall (Ragga Bomb) with an assist from Tigress and Randall Osbourne. Attacked Alex Extreme and Randall Osbourne with a chair before the bell of a scheduled three-way defense on 21 March 2004, then postponed the match to a cage bout the following week without it ever starting, citing his own father's recent death. Retained again in the rescheduled steel cage match on 5 May 2004: Osbourne never entered after Alex Kidd attacked him before the bell, and Legba climbed out of the cage to the arena floor ahead of the remaining challenger, Alex Extreme, to win by escape. Retained again on 19 May 2004, teaming with Tigress to beat Simon O'Neal and Donna Tetreault in an intergender tag after a top-rope splash caught both opponents for the pin.

title: uwf-mar96-rampage-championship
label: "Showtime" Rick Marley

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 16 October 2004: "Showtime" Rick Marley pinned champion Jamie Underwood with a small package after Underwood turned his back on the match to check on his own distracted "son."

note: Won the UWF Rampage Championship from Jamie Underwood in his own first UWF match, catching the champion looking away from the match. The upset touched off Underwood's own violent falling-out with his "son," who turned out to be the biological child of a returning Sabbath. Retained again over Brian McKenzie by countout on 30 October 2004, after McKenzie abandoned the match to save tag partner Chris O'Brien from a backstage beating by Michael Bonn. Retained again over "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath in a no-contest on 27 November 2004, after Jamie Underwood interfered with a steel chair. Retained again over "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas by pinfall (the Limelight) on 11 December 2004, aided by Jason Keening's own distracting presence at ringside.

lost.source: The promotion's own commentary on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 May 2005, recapping that Marcus Nuit won the title from Rick Marley at the Rise to Power pre-show; that pre-show itself has no primary-source card text in the held record.

title: uwf-mar96-womens-heavyweight-championship-of-the-world
label: Donna Tetreault

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 May 2004: Donna Tetreault pinned champion Stephanie Harper after a somersault plancha caught both Harper and cornerman Simon O'Neal, dragging Harper back into the ring for the cover as the referee's ten count on both women lapsed.

note: Won the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World from Stephanie Harper in a career-first title win; a pair of brass knuckles was found at ringside afterward, though no one openly claimed them. Teamed with cornerman Simon O'Neal on 19 May 2004 in a losing challenge for the UWF Meltdown Championship against Tigress and champion Papa Legba, whose top-rope splash caught them both; the Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World was not at stake in that match. Retained against Stephanie Harper again at Gold Rush 2004 (5 June 2004), using brass knuckles and then a foreign object hidden in her own bandana for the Caress of Steel; knocked out manager Simon O'Neal after he proposed marriage to her in the ring afterward. Retained again over Brianna Landis by pinfall (the Dominion Day windmill suplex) on 18 September 2004, aided by a distraction belt shot from Landis's own tag partner, Tara "Sunburst" Marshall. Retained again over "Battle Princess" Misaki Ishikawa by disqualification on 16 October 2004, after Ishikawa was found with a taser at ringside despite having the champion beaten clean moments earlier. Retained again over Kari Stevens by submission (a crossface, with salt and lemon juice rubbed into a cut over Stevens's own eye) on 30 October 2004.

lost.source: Sierra Browne's own backstage interview on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 May 2005, stating she beat Donna Tetreault for the title at Rise to Power with ownership shares also on the line; that pre-show itself has no primary-source card text in the held record.

Retained again over Quinn Brown by pinfall (a high-elevation Death Valley Driver) on 13 November 2004, after Roxy Mayhem pulled fellow Violence Girl Simone Sumner into Brown's path to save him from a missile dropkick. Retained again over Uriah Hawkins by pinfall on 17 November 2004, hanging onto the top rope as Hawkins drove his own head into the mat attempting a Suicide DDT.

lost.source: the promotion's own billing of a new North American Heavyweight Champion by the UWF Meltdown of 8 June 2005; no surviving document in the held record states the match.

title: uwf-mar96-cruiserweight-championship-of-the-world
label: One-Winged Angel

won.source: UWF Gold Rush 2004, 5 June 2004: One-Winged Angel reversed champion Michael Bonn's own Deadfall attempt into an uranage, then finished with a top-rope Hell's Halo (moonsault elbow) for the pinfall.

note: Won the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World from Michael Bonn at Gold Rush 2004, a career-first title win in the held record; cornerwoman Ami Tran and Amity stablemate Spice each ran interference at ringside during the match. Retained again over Youth Gone Wild by pinfall (a top-rope german release suplex) on 25 May 2005, a tightly wrestled, mutually respectful contest. Retained again over Vyolynce by disqualification on 11 June 2005, after Vyolynce refused to break a rope-break leg hold. Lost the title to Jacob Drake in a bout not read by this collection, recapped on commentary during UWF Meltdown, 20 July 2005.

lost.source: UWF Meltdown, 20 July 2005: commentary describes Jacob Drake upsetting One-Winged Angel for the Cruiserweight Championship of the World on the previous week's own unread Rampage (9 July 2005); no surviving document in the held record states the match itself.

title: uwf-mar96-meltdown-championship
label: Collision Holly

won.source: UWF Meltdown, 25 August 2004: Collision Holly pinned champion Papa Legba with a second-rope bulldog after absorbing a long beating.

note: Won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Papa Legba in a career-first title win, seconded to ringside by Rampage Champion Uriah Hawkins, who had encouraged him beforehand to treat the match seriously rather than as a showcase for the champion. Lost the title to Tigress by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 22 September 2004, after Vyolynce, the match's own advertised third participant, declined to compete and left the ring before the bell.

title: uwf-mar96-rampage-championship
label: Marcus Nuit

won.source: The promotion's own billing and commentary on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 28 May 2005, crediting Marcus Nuit with winning the title from Rick Marley at the Rise to Power pre-show; that pre-show itself has no primary-source card text in the held record.

note: Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing and commentary; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which Nuit won the title from Rick Marley at the Rise to Power pre-show. Retained the title over "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath by pinfall (a headscissors takedown into a cradle) on 28 May 2005, his own first Rampage title defense, declaring himself the "Renegade of Rampage" beforehand. Retained again over the Mercenary by pinfall (a senton splash) on 11 June 2005, the title's own last defense before its unification with the Meltdown Championship the following week. title: uwf-mar96-north-american-tag-team-championship
label: The Amazing Romanis

won.source: UWF Meltdown, 20 October 2004: the Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos Romani) beat the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) by pinfall, Niklos pinning Lincoln with a neckbreaker off his own brother's shoulders after a returning Vyolynce's own ringside chair distraction.

note: Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship from the Universal Powers under a new team name, having previously wrestled together in this wing as the Arcana. Retained again over the Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) by pinfall (Without A Net) on 17 November 2004, aided by a mystery burst of pyrotechnics and an eyeball graphic that rattled Shadoe Rage ahead of the finish. A defense against the Hands of Death (Serge Annis, Caliban) on 1 December 2004 was thrown out as a no-contest after the arriving Prophets of Rage provoked a weapons brawl; the champions were hung by dog collars afterward, and both the Hands of Death and the winner of their own Rise to Power dog collar match with the Prophets of Rage were subsequently challenged to a title match by the champions themselves. Lost the titles to the Prophets of Rage in a bout not read by this collection, per the promotion's own billing on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 18 March 2006.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 18 March 2006: the Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) are billed as reigning North American Tag Team Champions, defending against Don't Go There; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which they took the titles from the Amazing Romanis.

title: uwf-mar96-womens-tag-team-championship
label: The Psychommunity

won.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 11 June 2005: Misaki Ishikawa signed a UWF contract and introduced older sister Naomi as her new partner, continuing the Women's Tag Team Championship reign in place of the departing Reona Yoshida without a title match.

note: Installed as champions on 11 June 2005 continuing the same reign in Reona Yoshida's place, rather than through a title match; retained the same night over the Love Sisters by pinfall (a Death Valley Bomb on Lolita Love), after the Love Sisters had been ambushed backstage beforehand by Moira Faith and "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict.

lost.source: Naomi Ishikawa pinned by the Misfits (a Spiked Mischief Maker) at Brawl From The Mall 6, Prophets of Rage member Shadoe Rage interfering to help finish the fall.

title: uwf-mar96-meltdown-championship

note: Won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Collision Holly in what was billed as a three-way submissions match; Vyolynce refused to participate and left the ring before the bell, leaving Tigress to beat Holly alone. Retained again over Youth Gone Wild by submission (an inverted dragon sleeper) on 6 October 2004. Retained again over Bobby Nash by pinfall (the Sumatran Headhunter, using the ropes for leverage) on 20 October 2004. Retained again over "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn by disqualification on 3 November 2004, after a UWF tryout group led by a disguised T.D. Swagger ran in. Retained again over Scorpio by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 17 November 2004. A defense against Scott "Hotspot" Daniels on 1 December 2004 ended in a double disqualification draw after both wrestlers fouled each other simultaneously; the title did not change hands. A defense against Marissa Monet on 25 May 2005 also ended in a double disqualification, after both wrestlers shoved the referee; the title did not change hands. Retained again over Marissa Monet by submission (a modified Marjara Mallaka surfboard) in a No DQ rematch on 8 June 2005, the title's own last defense before its unification with the Rampage Championship the following week. Lost the title to Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit by pinfall (the 51st Drop) in a title unification match on 22 June 2005, ending the Meltdown Championship's own separate history.

lost.source: UWF Meltdown, 22 June 2005: Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit pinned Tigress with the 51st Drop in a title unification match, and the Meltdown Championship was retired into the new Unified Television Championship.

title: uwf-mar96-rampage-championship
label: Paul Wong

won.source: the promotion's own billing on Saturday Night Rampage, 9 August 2003

Retained against Tom Landis (9 August 2003) and Cameron Black (30 August 2003) before losing the title to the One-Winged Angel by pinfall on 4 October 2003.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 4 October 2003: pinned by the One-Winged Angel with a top-rope moonsault elbowdrop (Hell's Halo).
